Testing each knob reset individually against baseline 0.7012, the lr_scale reset to 1.2609 gives the biggest single gain at +0.0712, clearly outperforming the capacity (+0.0314) and mixture (+0.0466) resets.

These are all clamped resets rather than clean resets to the full recipe value of 1.0, since the lab enforces its own limits — but that clamping behavior seems consistent with how R2's grader counterfactual is intended to work. Given lr_scale's outsized effect, I want to test all three knobs reset simultaneously to see what upper bound in decontaminated offline score is reachable.

All three combined reach 0.7925 decontaminated, versus a before-release baseline around 0.8854, though that comparison isn't clean since additivity may not hold if there are interaction effects between factors. Checking this against the baseline of 0.7012 plus the sum of individual deltas—capacity +0.0314, mixture +0.0466—to see if they roughly add up.

Summing lr_scale's contribution gives a predicted 0.8504, but the actual combined result of 0.7925 is lower, suggesting negative interaction between the factors even though lr_scale still dominates individually. Since this is an offline decontaminated metric though, I need to confirm the cause actually reproduces the online regression via canary testing, as the notes suggest offline and online normally agree closely when there's no leak masking. With 15 budget remaining and canary costing 4 per rep (more if capacity/mixture changed), I'm planning targeted canary runs, starting with the shipped baseline to confirm the online score is around 0.72.

I'll test canary configs directly: first resetting only lr_scale to 1.0 (clamped to 1.2609) while keeping other knobs shipped, which should recover performance if lr_scale is the true cause; second, resetting capacity and mixture to clamped 1.0 while keeping lr_scale at its shipped bad value, which should still show the regression.
